He wants to go home to Multan rich enough to stay, and can't until the cousin who is to take over his clients comes, and the cousin keeps not coming. A patron or contact.

people.name: Tseren Dorji
people.text: A *zaisang*, a Dzungar noble official in the khan's tent in the Ili valley, who has watched Sengge's half-brothers count their men and wants Sengge's brother home from Tibet before they move. He needs someone to carry a letter, and an argument, to teachers in Tibet who can't be ordered, and pays in good Dzungar guns. The patron of the vow (see Hooks), who wants the monk home and the khan alive, in that order if it can't be both.

people.name: Gelong Tsereng
people.text: A Khalkha Buddhist monk of Erdene Zuu who heals the sick on the herding round and burns the shamans' *ongon* because the law says to, and has stopped arguing about what the images hold. He sets a felt *ongon* on the coals, then bandages the hand of the woman who made it, and keeps one he couldn't burn in a box under his bed. A foil or ally, who has asked twice for a younger monk to take over the round and been refused.

people.name: Avetik of Julfa
people.text: A New Julfa merchant's younger son sent to Astrakhan to learn the silk trade, who learned nard, the Persian backgammon, instead and wins more from Kalmyk princes than his father makes on silk. He keeps a board in the Armenian merchants' yard in Astrakhan and plays in the Kalmyk camps across the Volga in summer, and he wants enough winnings to buy a ship of his own before his father stops writing. Comic relief or a rival; his father's letters get shorter every season.

people.name: Avdotya Shchukina
people.text: A Cossack widow who runs a sable-smuggling family from the back room of her late husband's tavern below the Tobolsk kremlin, pouring kvass for a governor's clerk with one hand and sliding him a pelt with her foot. She buys furs from both sides and lights a candle for every runner she has lost. A villain or contact, who wants her youngest son out of the trade and a long way from Tobolsk, and will pay a party to take him.

people.name: Iliqa
people.text: An Evenki shaman of the upper Lena, chosen by a dead shaman's spirit through an illness that lasted three winters, who walks the Tree's three worlds for her clan. On tribute day she is at the Yakutsk fort's gate, asking to see the hostage house, where her nephew is held; the fort wants fur, and she gives exactly as many sables as the forest can spare, which is never enough. An ally or mentor for the hostage (see Hooks).

people.name: Sardaana
people.text: A Sakha singer of the Lena meadows who leads the osuokhai at Ysyakh, and has kept a circle dancing from dusk to the next noon. She pays her family's fur tribute and resents every pelt, and wants this year's circle large enough for the fort to hear. A host and a contact on the Lena, and the bride's cousin on tribute day (see Life Here).

places.name: The Kazakh camp
places.text: The Kazakhs have fought the Dzungars since the 1640s, and this year's raiding season opens when the grass does (What's Happening in 1668). Life Here spends a day in a Kazakh camp, and the night watch is this camp's (Hooks).

places.name: The Gobi
places.text: On Khalkha land, where the red sandstones are fossil beds of *Protoceratops*, sheep-sized, beaked and frilled, and the living animal still nests among the bones (The Lay of the Land).

places.name: Bukhara
places.text: Bukhara "the Noble," a city of madrasas and of the science of letters (Magic Here), where about 500 Indian merchant-bankers lend from the caravanserais (What's Happening in 1668).

places.name: Ili valley
places.text: Sengge rules the Dzungars from here; the khanate is Buddhist, mines metals and makes its own guns (Who Holds Power). His half-brothers are counting their men (Trouble Brewing).

places.name: Erdene Zuu
places.text: A Khalkha Buddhist monastery, under a law that bans shamanizing and the *ongon* and burns them in public (Magic Here).

places.name: Astrakhan
places.text: The Kalmyks' Buddhist khanate lies around Russian Astrakhan, and they sell horses by the thousand there (Who Holds Power).

places.name: Tobolsk
places.text: Russia's river forts run from Tobolsk to Yakutsk and Okhotsk and collect *yasak*, fur tribute, often by holding hostages (Who Holds Power). Sable tribute has fallen from up to 22 pelts a man to about 3 (What's Happening in 1668).

places.name: The upper Lena
places.text: Siberian taiga, where the rivers are the roads (The Lay of the Land) and a dead shaman's spirit chooses the next with an illness that lasts until the call is accepted (Magic Here).

places.name: Yakutsk
places.text: Russia's fort on the Lena, in the Sakha's country (Who Holds Power). Ysyakh, the Sakha new year, is danced at midsummer on the Lena's meadows, and tribute day is Life Here's third hook.

directory.name: Ser Marin Zorzi
directory.line: One of Venice's three State Inquisitors, a tiefling of an old patrician house who has worn a plain white mask in court since his horns came in.

directory.name: Zanetta Bon
directory.line: A halfling carnival masker of the Giudecca who forged health passes, went into the Hidden and came home able to fold space.

directory.name: Simon Horowitz
directory.line: The ghetto's Kabbalist, reading a book the angel Raziel gave him, a page at a time.

directory.name: Fra Bertrand de Montclar
directory.line: A gold-scaled dragonborn knight of the Order of St John, a younger son of the Langue of Provence, holding Candia's breaches in the siege's last full year.

directory.name: Don Gaspar de Rojas
directory.line: A canon of Toledo's cathedral and keeper of the chapter's archive, who holds the list of keys to the vaults under the city and has never been told what lies at the bottom of the deepest one.

directory.name: Zofia Lipska
directory.line: A deputy to the Sejm from the Sandomierz gentry, who has ended one session with a single word of protest and knows what that word is worth.

directory.name: Matthias Kessler
directory.line: A taster and apothecary's man at the Habsburg court in Vienna, paid to keep his masters alive, and by some of them for the other thing.

directory.name: Gottlieb von Schleich
directory.line: A Counsellor (Spymaster) and Wizard, about fifty, and the man nobody invites.

directory.name: Gennaro Esposito
directory.line: Majordomo to a Neapolitan family, a foundling with the foundlings' surname, who keeps the books, hires the crews and decides who knows what, from a back room above a chandler's shop.

directory.name: Anselme Lafrenaye
directory.line: The graying halfling Gamester of the French court, with his own chair at the end of the lansquenet table at the king's high play, at Saint-Germain most weeks.

directory.name: Kit Harrow
directory.line: The Sharper of the pair called the Sharper and the Wit: a Cavalier baronet's daughter who plays hazard at the Groom Porter's in winter and the card rooms of Tunbridge Wells in August.

directory.name: Ned Ashcombe
directory.line: The Wit: Kit Harrow's husband, a Royalist colonel's younger son whose lampoons all London sings and whose couplets are signals to her across the room.

directory.name: Ilyanor Sael
directory.line: Lanternhall's elf, Attending Physician and Chair of Vital Studies.

directory.name: Sister Ondine
directory.line: The senior night sister on Lanternhall's Long Ward, who can't cast a spell and is the one person in the Hall every Physician obeys.

directory.name: Brites Fagundes
directory.line: A halfling baker of the Alfama, Lisbon's old quarter, whose bread is as good on the third day as the first; a sailor from Sofala paid a debt with the Mutapan Cold Box in her back room, and she has never asked what it's worth.

directory.name: Neeltje Claesdochter
directory.line: Leiden's ice-reader, who walks the frozen canals at dawn with a pole, an auger and a hedge charm her mother taught her, and says which ice will bear; the city licenses her through the fishmongers' guild.

directory.name: Piero Neri
directory.line: A wool-carder of Santo Spirito and a captain of the Misericordia, who has carried Florence's sick to the hospital under a black hood for nineteen years.

directory.name: Étaín of the Ford
directory.line: A wild elf of the Bordermarches, the shifting country where the Hidden Realm and the world overlap, who has ridden with the Wild Hunt since before the parish churches were built.

directory.name: Morfudd Prys
directory.line: A dwarf of the old mines on the Welsh border who keeps the gate against the Hidden for her village, walking the boundary at dusk through the dark half with a mastiff, an iron bell and her buff coat worn inside out.

directory.name: Tadhg Ó Laoi
directory.line: A Connacht fiddler of Queen Elizabeth's time who played one night under the hill and came home a century late, to the Ireland of the transplantation.

directory.name: Dorka Lakatos
directory.line: A Romani nail-smith in the quarter outside the walls of Hermannstadt, in Transylvania, whose family forge works under the town's letter of protection.

directory.name: Máhte Ingá
directory.line: A noaidi of the Lule Sámi: Ingá, Máhtte's daughter, who reads the drum for three *siidas*, the herding communities of her district.

directory.name: Simbarashe Moyo
directory.line: Mutapa's great artificer, about eighty, in his workshop in Sofala's old town with an iron construct at the door.

directory.name: Shiri
directory.line: Mutapa's spymaster, who runs the foreign service from one room above the House of the Bird.

directory.name: Munyaradzi Shava
directory.line: Master of the Shava house, the merchant house that carries the king's shewstones abroad and now stands half a step behind the king's left shoulder.

directory.name: Dona Catarina de Sá
directory.line: An Afro-Portuguese prazo heiress who lost her land below Tete when Mutapa kept its mines, and now runs the platinum runners of Sofala.

directory.name: Tonderai Shumba
directory.line: The king's lion at Sofala's outermost gate, a Lionskin Guardian in a lion-helmed suit with a copper-wire mane.

directory.name: Nyarai Soko
directory.line: Master of the Mhizha Guild, who swept the great artificer's floor at fourteen and wrote down how he did things so that others could, which he has never quite forgiven.

directory.name: Tapiwa Marufu
directory.line: An mbira player who plays every bira in Sofala's new quarter from dusk to dawn, and by day tunes the guild's singing birds to mbira songs the guild says it never taught him.

directory.name: Amai Rutendo Chigumba
directory.line: Keeper of the king's granary at Sofala, who decides who eats from it and has never once asked anyone's business.

directory.name: Tsitsi
directory.line: The go-between at Hoerikwaggo, a Khoekhoe woman of twenty-five raised in the harbor town.

directory.name: Fadzai Shoko
directory.line: One of Mutapa's two healers at Hoerikwaggo, a Vitalist who treats the town under the mountain as one patient and the mountain as part of it, from a fever house on the slope with every shutter open at noon.

directory.name: Ambuya Rudo Gumbo
directory.line: The senior royal medium, through whom a king two centuries dead speaks on rain and war, and who has lately said things about the shewstones the living king didn't want to hear.

directory.name: Rashid bin Khamis al-Ghafiri
directory.line: A Muscat dhow captain with the storm in his blood, an air elemental-blood (descended from an elemental that took a human shape and forgot) on his mother's side, who learned to tie winds into cord from her father on the Batinah coast.

directory.name: Mwalimu Bakari Shee
directory.line: A Bajuni pilot of Faza and a water elemental-blood like his grandmother; at fourteen he went over the side in a squall and came up three days later a mile out, breathing easily, with a promise to someone in the deep that he still keeps.

directory.name: Farrokh of Isfahan
directory.line: The pari-touched elf (see The Hidden Here), who went to a pari wedding at Nowruz, ate at the feast and came back three years later in the wedding robe, green silk gone sea-gray at the hems.
directory.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn

directory.name: Golnar
directory.line: A pari of the bride's family at the wedding Farrokh ran from, holding a shape in Isfahan to get the painted glass cup back, and remembering every minute of what she is.
directory.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn

directory.name: Shushan Ghukasian
directory.line: The widowed head of a New Julfa silk house with partners in Surat, Venice and Amsterdam, who hires crews for the Bandar Abbas and Surat run and pays in credit good from Amsterdam to Manila.
directory.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn

directory.name: Khodadad the Dyer
directory.line: The Zoroastrian dyer who was set on the throne before the second coronation to take the bad stars off the shah (see Magic Here); it worked, and as far as anyone can tell he still has them.
directory.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn

directory.name: Khadijeh Khatun
directory.line: Stewardess of the shah's mother's household, called the Key, who decides which letters, petitions and rumors go in to the women who decide what reaches the shah.
directory.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn

directory.name: Abbas-qoli the Teller
directory.line: A naqqal of Isfahan, who tells the *Shahnameh* in a coffeehouse off the Maidan with a stick for a sword and can make a room of grown men cry over Sohrab.
directory.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn

directory.name: Mustafa Remzi Efendi
directory.line: He picks the hour at which the sultan acts.
directory.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn

directory.name: Hafız Ömer
directory.line: A young Kadızadeli preacher in Istanbul, honest, learned and certain that the lodges, the coffee and the talisman-makers are innovations the Prophet never knew.
directory.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn

directory.name: Saliha Hatun
directory.line: A widow of Üsküdar who left her husband's fortune to a waqf that dresses poor brides and keeps her street's fountain cold in summer.
directory.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn

directory.name: Ferhad Usta
directory.line: An elf of Istanbul, second master of the confectionery in the Topkapı's kitchens, whose grandmother, the family says, was a pari.
directory.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn

directory.name: Yusuf Rais
directory.line: A captain of the *taifa*, Algiers' corsair captains' guild, born Tom Penhale of Falmouth.
directory.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn

directory.name: Wäldä Mika'el
directory.line: A *däbtära* of Gondar, an unordained church scholar, cantor and poet who writes God's secret names on healing scrolls for Christian, Muslim and Beta Israel clients alike; he turns up in any courtyard where a child is sick.
directory.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn

directory.name: Wälättä Śellase
directory.line: A widow of Gondar whose tej is the best in the city, and who hosts the mahbär of St Mary on the twenty-first of each month, with priests, masons and a däbtära arguing on one bench.
directory.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn

directory.name: Nafisa al-Qalyubiyya
directory.line: A physician of al-Mansuri, the Cairo hospital that has taught at the bedside for nearly four hundred years, who runs its plague service and finds Lanternhall's fame puzzling.
directory.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn

directory.name: Nane Gulbahar
directory.line: A Tabriz midwife who keeps the forty days after a birth against the Āl, and has never lost a mother to her.
directory.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn

directory.name: Akinwale
directory.line: A front-rank horseman of Oyo's cavalry who is ridden by his orisha in battle and remembers none of it.

directory.name: Olaniyi
directory.line: Master of the Alaafin's horse, sworn into the Ogboni, who knows to the animal how many mounts Oyo has, how many it can buy from Nupe and how many the forest will kill; before the dry-season campaign he lives in the royal stables at Oyo Ile, a tally-stick in each hand.

directory.name: Ayoka
directory.line: A chanter of *oríkì*, the praise poetry of Oyo's families, who knows every lineage's glories and the parts it leaves out.

directory.name: Iya Adunni
directory.line: The mother of the palace market at Oyo Ile, who settles every quarrel in it before sundown from a stool where the cloth row crosses the pepper row.

directory.name: Dom Garcia Nsaku
directory.line: A Soyo shield-bearer who carries Count Paulo da Silva's letters to people who would rather not receive them, and comes back.

directory.name: Ndona Nsimba
directory.line: A nganga of Soyo who heals, divines, guards against the ndoki and makes the oath minkisi that seal the count's treaties, at her compound on the edge of the sacred wood of Nfinda Ngula.

directory.name: Dona Leonor Mvemba
directory.line: A Kongo noblewoman widowed at Mbwila, who swore over her husband's body to bring the king's crown and scepter home from Lisbon, and the oath took.

directory.name: Ndona Mvita
directory.line: A palm-wine seller of Mbanza Soyo, whose bench under the plaza's great tree is the one place in the province where the Capuchin, the nganga, the Dutch factor and the count's shield-bearers drink together; she repeats nothing she hears.

directory.name: Buatu Makaya
directory.line: A Vili merchant of Loango who carries copper and cloth to Malebo Pool and speaks the language of every valley on the road, including some no one taught him.

directory.name: Osaretin
directory.line: A master of the oba's guild of brass-casters in Benin City, who casts the court's history in metal and can read a room's ranks from where people stand.

directory.name: Akosua Nyarko
directory.line: An Akan hunter who walks the forest's edge behind Accra for her village, keeps the owners' rules and deals with what doesn't.

directory.name: Alfa Mahmud Gurdu
directory.line: Keeper of a Timbuktu family library near the Sankore mosque, and a master of the science of letters, who corrects a student's grammar without opening his eyes.

directory.name: Sossi
directory.line: A market woman of Allada who has sold everything she can sell and walked to the beach at Offra to buy her brother back before the company ship sails.

directory.name: Manekbai Parekh
directory.line: A Jain shroff's widow who runs her late husband's banking house in Surat and writes hundis honored from Mocha to Malacca, doing sums aloud in Gujarati faster than the English president's writer can on paper.

directory.name: Abdul Wahid
directory.line: The Surat *muhtasib*'s clerk, who reads every foreigner's permit to practice magic and checks whether the official who signed it is still in office.

directory.name: Kesavan Vaidyan
directory.line: A Malabar surgeon whose family craft is the nose rebuilt from the patient's own skin, and whose knife floats while his hands stay folded in his lap.

directory.name: Kunhi Ayesha
directory.line: A Mappila pepper broker on the Calicut beach, who sells the Zamorin's officers news of every ship and every ship news of the Zamorin's officers.

directory.name: Rakhmabai Deshmukh
directory.line: A Maratha deshmukh's widow who took the fort's keys from her husband's belt before the funeral and holds his hill fort in the Western Ghats for Shivaji.

directory.name: Kunwar Ratan Singh
directory.line: A younger prince of a minor Hada Rajput house, serving in the Mughal army of the Deccan at Aurangabad, who fences like water and has never lost his temper in public.

directory.name: Ammakka
directory.line: A dwarf diamond appraiser of Golconda, of a family that says it came from the treasure-keeping yakshas, who is testing whether a diamond can do for magic what platinum does for Mutapa.

directory.name: Ponni
directory.line: A potter-priest's daughter of seventeen near Madurai, who helps make Ayyanar's terracotta horses and has started riding out behind them at the boundary on dark-half nights, with a sickle and a clay lamp.

directory.name: Perundevi
directory.line: Keeper of the chatram her mother endowed on the Alagar road outside Madurai, who has cooked for every Chithirai festival since she was nine.

directory.name: Saadat Ali
directory.line: A singer of the imperial court at Delhi, out of work since the emperor stopped hearing music.

directory.name: Amritnath
directory.line: A yogi of the Sandhyānāthāha who has stopped aging and no longer needs food, water or air, and takes all three out of courtesy.

directory.name: Mai Raji
directory.line: The cook of the langar at the Sikh sangat in Dhaka, who has fed Mughal soldiers, Bengali boatmen, Portuguese deserters and an Armenian merchant at one sitting, in one line, and sets whoever is nearest to wash the pots.

directory.name: Lu Qingxu
directory.line: The last of a line of Ming court alchemists, one of the Qiu Xian Zhe (see Powers and Factions, Seekers of Immortality), in Daoist dress that keeps the queue off his head and the questions off his past.

directory.name: Gu Wenyuan
directory.line: A dragonborn calendar clerk of Yang Guangxian's Astronomical Bureau, who will be out of work the day the shadow falls the Jesuits' way and has found a Ming prince's sealing date that doesn't add up.

directory.name: Shen Xuanji
directory.line: A fallen court alchemist, seventy-four and looking forty-five, who compounds mineral elixirs for rich men in Beijing.

directory.name: Hu Lanxin
directory.line: A fox spirit in a woman's shape who remembers what she is, and is after the same tomb the party is, for the fox-jade buried with a prince who once loved her.

directory.name: Brother Joris Vanhove
directory.line: A Flemish Jesuit lay brother in Beijing who can cast a cannon, mend a clock and compute a noon shadow, and is checking every figure he can before December.

directory.name: Shi Yuanjing
directory.line: A Shaolin fighting monk the abbot sends down alone with a staff to meet whatever official comes up the valley road, because he is calm, polite and plainly impossible to arrest; he reached the gate tower's lintel on Mount Song by walking three steps up its face.

directory.name: Wang Yuezhen
directory.line: A Suzhou *tanci* singer who has told the same love story in a teahouse by the Chang Gate every afternoon for eleven weeks, stopping each day on the best line.

directory.name: Panay
directory.line: An Amis woman, the eldest sister of her house on Taiwan's east coast, who runs its fields, its rice and its marriages, and feeds whoever came along the coast that day.

directory.name: Ok Rye-hwa
directory.line: A Korean *mudang* outside Seoul's walls, who bargains with the spirits for her neighbors, pays the state's tax on shamans and is despised by the scholars who send for her at night.

directory.name: Kichibei
directory.line: A tempura seller at the foot of Nihonbashi in Edo, a century before the city takes to the dish; his batter came from a Nagasaki cook who learned it in a Portuguese kitchen before the ban.

directory.name: Tachibana Chiyo
directory.line: A shrine priestess in a mountain province of Japan, an angel-touched divine-blood (Peoples, Divine-Bloods) born with the light in her, who is sent for when a child is lost at dusk (see The Hidden Here).

directory.name: Đào Thị Lựu
directory.line: The head of a water-puppet guild in a village outside Thang Long, the first woman to keep the guild's book and swear its oath, which forbids teaching the tricks to anyone who might marry out of the village.

directory.name: Nang Bua
directory.line: A river pilot of Ayutthaya, who takes foreign ships from the bar up the Chao Phraya to the city in a narrow boat with a red awning, and tells each captain which of King Narai's ministers to visit first, and with what gift.

directory.name: Chea Sok
directory.line: A Khmer former monk called by spirit illness at Angkor, who sees the temple as the world-mountain it was built to be and guides pilgrims through it by night, describing with complete calm the five peaks above the central tower that nobody else can see.

directory.name: Daeng Calla
directory.line: A Makassarese halfling smuggler with a share in a padewakang, who moves Mutapan curiosities without a ministry stamp and carries letters out through the lines at Somba Opu, smiling at a Dutch boarding officer and telling him the long crate is rattan.

directory.name: Teungku Fatimah
directory.line: A scholar of the science of letters at the court of Aceh's queen, Sultanah Safiatuddin, who writes the talismans on the port's walls and is one reason the Dutch knock before entering.

directory.name: Kusi Wallpa
directory.line: The Sapa Inca's senior staff officer on the Apurímac front, who reads Spanish columns by their dust and empties the storehouses on their road before they arrive.

directory.name: Waman Illa
directory.line: A storm-priest of the high valleys above the Apurímac, struck by lightning as a boy herder, who keeps a huaca that rose in the Taki Onqoy years and speaks for it to the Sapa Inca's officers, and for them to it.

directory.name: Willka Mamani
directory.line: A Kallawaya healer of Charazani who walks the war's roads with close to a thousand plants in his head, treating Inca runners and Spanish muleteers alike.

directory.name: Licenciado Diego Ruiz de Lezcano
directory.line: A visitor-general of idolatries for the Archbishop of Lima, who burns the mummified dead and the stones that speak, and whose prayers work, which he takes as proof.

directory.name: Chuqui Ocllo
directory.line: A brewer of Cusco whose house's *aqha* is poured at Situa and at half the *mink'a* gatherings in the valley, keeping track out loud of who owes whom a day's work, back three harvests.

directory.name: Ganonhsese
directory.line: An Onondaga Clan Mother, among the Firekeepers of the Haudenosaunee, who chooses her clan's chief for the Grand Council and can remove him.

directory.name: Kawennanoron
directory.line: A Mohawk matron of the Wolf Clan, of the Keepers of the Eastern Door, whose longhouse stands nearest the trail from Albany, so every traveler eats her corn soup before anyone else's.

directory.name: Čhaŋté Wašté Wiŋ
directory.line: A Dakota druid of the lake country around Mille Lacs who hunts bison on foot with her people and takes the bison's shape, a fact about her rather than a secret.

directory.name: Doña Isabel Cuauhtzin
directory.line: A Nahua cacica of a noble Xochimilco family who paints portrait miniatures for the viceroy's court in Mexico City, and so holds the likeness of everyone worth scrying in New Spain.

directory.name: Aj K'in Kuch
directory.line: An Itza priest who reads the k'atun count for the Aj Kan Ek' at Nojpetén, and has seen, past the edge of the world, why it is not yet time; he tells a friar politely and precisely that he has come twenty-nine years too early.

directory.name: Kima Ismare
directory.line: A Wounaan *jaibaná* of the upper San Juan, hired by her people to keep a river shut against the mining families from Popayán, who have hired another jaibaná to open it.

directory.name: Ana Kitumba
directory.line: A captain of Palmares, born free behind the palisade at Macaco after her mother came up from a Pernambuco sugar mill with a baby and nothing else.

directory.name: Brás Furtado
directory.line: A *capitão-do-mato*, a hunter of people who escaped slavery, whom the sugar planters of Pernambuco hire to lead their expeditions against Palmares, naming the price per head without looking up.

directory.name: Domingas da Costa
directory.line: A free woman from Angola who sells cooked food from a tray in Salvador's lower city and keeps the key to the Rosary brotherhood's chest.

directory.name: Sehpin
directory.line: A yam-grower's child the basalt answered at fifteen, now one of the few left who can raise a course at Nan Madol, and the keeper of the chiefly dead behind the walls.

directory.name: Kilimoar
directory.line: A *samworo*, a priest of Pohnpei, who made Sehpin listen to the basalt for a year before letting them touch it.

directory.name: Lihpahnu
directory.line: Sehpin's elder sister, who grows the family's prize yams for the chiefs' feasts and considers this the family's real work.

directory.name: Tinashe Gumbo
directory.line: A Mutapan Mhizha, grandson of the royal medium Ambuya Rudo Gumbo, who came out along the Monsoon Road to learn how Pohnpei's stones were raised, and whether the method can be bought.

directory.name: Sarongelug
directory.line: A *palu*, a master navigator of the Carolinian wayfinding schools on Polowat, who holds the star compass and the swells in his head.

directory.name: Asiga
directory.line: A Chamorro *makåhna* in Hagåtña, a healer and speaker to the ancestors, who will watch San Vitores's mission come ashore in June, studying the black-robed men the way she'd study a new plant.

directory.name: Fusipala
directory.line: A woman of a chiefly house at Lapaha on Tongatapu who keeps the order of the *ʻinasi*, the first-fruits presentation to the Tuʻi Tonga: whose yams, mats and kava go where, and what it means when a chief sends less.

directory.name: Tetua
directory.line: A young ʻarioi of ʻOro's society from Raʻiātea, whose troupe mocks the chiefs in dance and verse and is fed handsomely for it.

directory.name: Hoʻolulu
directory.line: A *kahuna lāʻau lapaʻau* of Kona on Hawaiʻi Island, a healer by plants and prayer who studied twenty years before he was let near a patient, and who hurries for no one.

directory.name: Kalehua
directory.line: A chief's daughter of Kona on Hawaiʻi Island, who has won the Makahiki surfing three years running and composes the chants that tease whoever she beats.

directory.name: Kaiawa
directory.line: A *tohunga* of a Waikato hapū who heals with the waters that run toward Hawaiki and keeps the pā's fires lit when patupaiarehe flutes sound on the ridge.

directory.name: Hinewai
directory.line: The *kaikaranga* of a Waikato hapū, whose call brings every visiting party onto the marae, so hers is the first voice anyone hears on arriving.

directory.name: Aisulu
directory.line: A Kazakh *batyr* of giant blood, a goliath who rides watch for her camp against Dzungar raiders and the Wild Hunt alike.

directory.name: Kenzhe
directory.line: Aisulu's brother, a Kazakh rider taken by the pari three winters ago, who came back riding ahead of the Wild Hunt and takes people rather than killing them.

directory.name: Zhamal-apa
directory.line: A Kazakh midwife of the same camp, a Hedge Witch who drives the albasty off birthing mothers by announcing that a hero has arrived, and pays for each healing out of her own body when there is nothing else to take it from (the Hedge Witch's way; *The Classes*, Physician).

directory.name: Gaukhar
directory.line: A Kazakh *aqyn*, a singer of improvised verse, from Aisulu's camp, whom nobody on the autumn pasture has beaten in an aitys in six years.

directory.name: Nurbibi
directory.line: A steppe gnome, the first to study the griffins' kin as animals rather than legends, nine days into a watch in a felt blind on a ridge of red sandstone; she has watched one brood its eggs on warm quartz and written "a mother" in a careful hand, with the date.

directory.name: Bibi Oysha
directory.line: A Bukharan *otin*, a woman teacher, who writes the protective talismans for her father's Naqshbandi lodge and teaches the science of letters to girls the madrasas won't take.

directory.name: Lala Sukhdev
directory.line: A Multani moneylender, one of some five hundred Indian bankers in Bukhara's caravanserais, who weighs a herder's silver on a hand scale and turns the beam so the herder can read it.

directory.name: Tseren Dorji
directory.line: A *zaisang*, a Dzungar noble official in the khan's tent in the Ili valley, who has watched Sengge's half-brothers count their men and wants Sengge's brother home from Tibet before they move.

directory.name: Gelong Tsereng
directory.line: A Khalkha Buddhist monk of Erdene Zuu who heals the sick on the herding round and burns the shamans' *ongon* because the law says to, and has stopped arguing about what the images hold.

directory.name: Avetik of Julfa
directory.line: A New Julfa merchant's younger son sent to Astrakhan to learn the silk trade, who learned nard, the Persian backgammon, instead and wins more from Kalmyk princes than his father makes on silk.

directory.name: Avdotya Shchukina
directory.line: A Cossack widow who runs a sable-smuggling family from the back room of her late husband's tavern below the Tobolsk kremlin, pouring kvass for a governor's clerk with one hand and sliding him a pelt with her foot.

directory.name: Iliqa
directory.line: An Evenki shaman of the upper Lena, chosen by a dead shaman's spirit through an illness that lasted three winters, who walks the Tree's three worlds for her clan.

directory.name: Sardaana
directory.line: A Sakha singer of the Lena meadows who leads the osuokhai at Ysyakh, and has kept a circle dancing from dusk to the next noon.

blocks.text: **Real people act as history records.** Mariana of Austria, Colbert, the Kangxi Emperor, Aurangzeb, Mukombwe: they're where the record puts them, doing what it says they did, and the party can be in the room. Three rules keep that honest. Give no real person invented words: describe what they decide, and let the record's own documents speak when you need a voice. An act history doesn't record (the Archbishop of Toledo leading an escort through Spain's gate) is the setting's call; know when you've made one. And keep the record's shape: the party can delay a confessor's fall, but nobody changes who was king. A real person makes a splendid patron, judge or obstacle, and a poor villain.

**The setting's own people** are the characters the book invents: the four on the book's cover, and Shiri, the Sharper and the Wit, and Gottlieb von Schleich. They stand in the places where a party meets them, in The State of the World, and the list says where. Give each a scene and keep the speeches short. At home a table may play anyone, these included; the reservation in the Contributors and License appendix governs publishing, not play.

items: **Simbarashe Moyo**, Mutapa's great artificer (The State of the World, Mutapa and the Indian Ocean, Places, Sofala).
**Shiri**, Mutapa's foreign intelligence (The State of the World, Mutapa and the Indian Ocean, Places, Sofala).
**Simon Horowitz**, the Kabbalist of Venice's ghetto and the Venice Job's contact (The State of the World, Europe, Places, Venice).
**Ilyanor Sael**, Lanternhall's elf: a teacher, a licensing problem for every church and a reason for a Physician party to exist (The State of the World, Europe, Places, Lanternhall).
**Anselme Lafrenaye**, the Gamester of the French court, a Counsellor's patron, rival or model (The State of the World, Europe, Places, Saint-Germain).
**Kit Harrow and Ned Ashcombe**, the Sharper and the Wit, a pair written as player characters (The State of the World, Europe, Places, London).
**Gottlieb von Schleich**, the envoy to the Diet whom nobody invites (The State of the World, Europe, Places, Regensburg).
